mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate indicates monetary easing, which can lead to increased borrowing and investment, thus driving positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns despite falling FEDFUNDS, the hypothesis is falsified.

mechanism_narrative: A rising unemployment rate signals economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 returns as consumer spending and business investment decline.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 rises despite UNRATE exceeding 5%, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in employment and a drop in unemployment indicates a strong economy, boosting S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 doesn't rise with these labor trends, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production in late-cycle expansion may signal reduced corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns despite slowing INDPRO would falsify this.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing housing starts reflect strong consumer demand, positively influencing S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Negative S&P 500 returns with rising HOUST would invalidate this.

mechanism_narrative: A slowdown in GDP growth indicates reduced economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns despite slow GDP growth would refute this.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate alongside slow retail sales growth may indicate economic stress, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: Positive S&P 500 returns under these conditions would falsify the hypothesis.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation as indicated by CPIAUCSL can erode profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If S&P 500 rises with CPIAUCSL above 3%, the hypothesis is invalid.
